units.title: Stablecoin-native L1s
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: unexecuted sides
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 24 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1079 and L-1063. Cycle 24 measured which sides of the PoolManager's 387 conditional jumps the block producers of MegaETH, Monad and HyperEVM have executed in mined transactions (research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-producer-branch-coverage.work, out/<chainId>/branches.json, scripts/pyevm_cov.py; findings F-118, F-130 and F-120 in state/findings.json). Never executed by any of the three: donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480), clear (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319), settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:305-307), ERC-6909 transfer, transferFrom and approve (src/ERC6909.sol:25-56), the 512-bit path of four of the five compiled copies of FullMath.mulDiv, the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:43-52), the 100 percent fee branch (src/libraries/Pool.sol:311), and on HyperEVM every exact-output path (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:88-104, SqrtPriceMath.sol:54-72, :102-118, :158-178). The critic corrected one assumption: an ordinary account does not need to borrow 2^96 units from the PoolManager to reach the fallback. It can deploy its own token at an address below a real token, so its token is currency0, mint any amount, open a hookless pool against the real token at a price near MAX_SQRT_PRICE, add liquidity, and swap its own token in. A wrong word on that path pays out the real token, which the PoolManager holds for other pools. Task 1: build, with the solc-js 0.8.26 already used for research/network-risk/build, or as hand-assembled bytecode, one read-only driver that runs inside a single eth_call with state overrides against the real PoolManager address of each of the 21 networks: it puts token doubles at two chosen addresses, calls unlock, and inside the callback initializes a hookless pool, adds liquidity, runs one action, and returns every delta, the slot0 and liquidity words read through extsload, and the token balances. Cover at least these actions, each over a grid of prices (MIN_SQRT_PRICE+1, 2^64, 2^96, 2^128, 2^129, 2^158, 2^159, MAX_SQRT_PRICE-1), liquidity (1, 2^32, 2^64, 2^96, 2^127, the maxLiquidityPerTick of the spacing) and amounts (1, 2^64, 2^96, 2^97, 2^120, 2^126, 2^127-1): exact-input and exact-output swaps in both directions, with fees 0, 1, 500, 999,999 and 1,000,000; donate with both amounts, with one, and into a pool whose liquidity is 0 (expect the revert); clear with the exact credit and with a wrong amount; settleFor to a third address; mint, then ERC-6909 transfer, approve, transferFrom by a spender with a finite and with an infinite allowance, setOperator, and burn from another account. Record which jumpmap sides each case executes with pyevm_cov.py, and add cases until every side that cycle 24 lists as never executed and that does not need governance has run, or say why a side cannot be reached. Task 2: run the cases on every network's public endpoint and compare each returned word with the Ethereum answer and with research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py running the same bytecode. On Monad also run the PoolManager frames of the cases through the compiled harness of cycle 23 (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work) at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7. On MegaETH and HyperEVM eth_call does not reach the producer; say so and list for each case whether any mined transaction executed its sides. Task 3: check the results against arithmetic that does not come from src/. For each swap case compute, with Python integers and exact fractions, the constant product relations for the liquidity and prices of the case, and state for each returned amount whether the pool received at least, and paid at most, what the exact relation gives: the input rounded up, the output rounded down, the fee rounded up, the next price rounded in the pool's favour. For donate and the ERC-6909 cases state the conservation rule (sum of deltas, sum of balances) and check it. Report every case where the pool would pay more or receive less than the exact relation, with the words, even if all networks agree with each other. Task 4: for the fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, enumerate the boundary: the largest amount for which amount * sqrtPX96 still fits, the first for which it wraps, the cases where the product fits and numerator1 + product wraps (line 45), and amounts whose wrapped product divided by amount equals sqrtPX96 by coincidence, if any exist; prove or refute by search that no input passes the test at line 43 with a wrapped product. Run those inputs through Tasks 2 and 3.

Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1077 and L-1080. The block producers of MegaETH and HyperEVM are closed, Monad's validators run compiled code that eth_call never uses, and on mainnet none of the three has executed donate, clear, settleFor, an ERC-6909 transfer or approval, or (on HyperEVM) an exact-output swap on the PoolManager (findings F-118, F-130, F-120; research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-producer-branch-coverage.work). Mined blocks are the only evidence that reaches these producers without sending a transaction, and their public testnets are a second source of mined blocks. The critic queried on 2026-11-26: rpc.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/evm answers chain id 0x3e6 and 'hyperliquid evm Testnet', with no code at the mainnet PoolManager address; carrot.megaeth.com/rpc and timothy.megaeth.com/rpc answer chain id 0x18c7 and mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42. Task 1: on the HyperEVM testnet, both MegaETH testnets and the Monad testnet (find its public endpoints and chain id in Monad's documentation), find every contract whose runtime equals research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json after the immutable is masked: start from Uniswap's published testnet deployment tables if they list these networks, then search Initialize logs (topic 0xdd466e674ea557f56295e2d0218a125ea4b4f0f6f3307b95f85e6110838d6438) over the history that the endpoints serve, and take the emitting addresses. Record address, code hash, deployment block and the number of logs per event. Task 2: for each such contract, collect its mined transactions (the collector of research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-state-replay.work/scripts, or the parent-storage replay scripts/gdrive.py of research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-replay-eleven.work where no trace endpoint exists), replay them word by word against the model, and count the jumpmap sides they execute with pyevm_cov.py. List which of the sides never executed on mainnet they add, and give every mismatch in full. Task 3: say what ties each testnet's producer to the mainnet producer: client version strings on both, release notes, documentation on whether testnet runs the same sequencer or validator release, and for Monad which release the testnet validators run and whether it compiles contracts under the same rule as mainnet. Evidence from a testnet that runs different code is weaker; say how much weaker. Task 4: on mainnet, extend the search for the missing sides beyond the cycle 24 windows without wide log ranges being refused: Donate, ERC-6909 Transfer with neither side zero, Approval and OperatorSet logs on Monad through any public indexer or explorer API that needs no key, and swaps ending at a tick clamp. Replay whatever is found.

Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1078 and L-1071. Cycle 24 read that reth v2.11.0 runs transactions ahead of time to warm caches and, in one path, commits the result of such a run without running the transaction again when the reads it recorded still match (research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-storage-key-mapping.research.json, lead text and the cleared item on reth v2.11.0). On Ethereum reth is one client among several and a wrong commit forks it off. Tempo has one client, and Base, the other OP Stack chains, Celo, X Layer, Arc and MegaETH run reth-derived nodes for most or all blocks; bor (BlockSTM) on Polygon, Monad's optimistic execution and BNB Smart Chain's parallel paths reuse speculative results by the same idea. A PoolManager transaction depends on more than storage slots: its own native balance (SELFBALANCE at src/types/Currency.sol:92), the balanceOf answer of a token whose balance an earlier transaction of the block changed (src/PoolManager.sol:285 and :358), transient storage that must be empty at the start of the transaction (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol), the code of a hook created earlier in the block, and the original slot values that SSTORE gas and refunds are computed from. Task 1: for each client, find the code that reuses or commits a result computed before the transaction's final position in the block was known: reth v2.11.0 (the build the Ethereum endpoint reports), tempo v1.19.1 (commit a9d6748) and any tagged release that carries T14, base v1.5.6 and v1.6.0-rc.3, op-reth v2.8.1 and v2.10.0-rc.4, celo-reth, xlayer-reth, the published Arc node, mega-evm v1.7.4 and the public MegaETH replica source, bor v2.11.1 and v2.12.0-beta (core/blockstm and parallel_statedb.go), Monad v0.16.7 (optimistic execution and its merge step), BSC v1.8.2 and reth-bsc. For each, state exactly what the recorded read set contains (storage slots, account balance, nonce, code hash, code bytes, account existence, transient storage, block environment values, precompile answers), how a result is validated before commit, and whether block building and block validation both use the path. Task 2: for each input listed above that a PoolManager transaction depends on, decide from the code whether a change made by an earlier transaction of the same block invalidates the speculative result. Pay attention to these cases: a native transfer into the PoolManager by transaction A and a native settle or take by transaction B; a token transfer to the PoolManager in A and sync plus settle in B; a pool initialize in A and a swap of that pool in B; a hook deployed in A and called in B; an ERC-6909 mint in A and a burn in B; A reverting after its speculative run succeeded; and gas refunds that depend on a slot's original value. Give file and line for each answer. Task 3: mined evidence. On Tempo, Base, Unichain, Polygon, Monad and MegaETH, find blocks in which two or more transactions touch the same PoolManager pool, the same currency balance, or create a hook and use it (start from the replay windows of cycles 23 and 24), and compare the state the chain committed after the block (eth_getStorageAt and eth_getBalance at that block, eth_getProof where served) with a serial replay of the block's PoolManager transactions through the model from the parent block's storage. Report the number of such blocks per network, the number of words compared and every mismatch in full. Cycle 23's committed.py did this for traced post state on eight networks; say which networks and block shapes are new here, Tempo above all. Task 4: say for each network whether the node that answers debug_traceTransaction replays serially, so that a trace speaks for the serial result and the committed state for the producer's, or whether both come from one path.

Cycle 24 read that the Avalanche C-Chain at avalanchego 1.15.3 (commit 983815fd, libevm d398bc4dbe41) accepts a block before executing it: the SAE executor runs the transactions afterwards (saexec/execution.go:293-470), latest is the last accepted block, and safe and finalized lag by six blocks (cleared items of unit established-l1 in cycle 24). Every Avalanche result so far, the opcode battery included, came from eth_call at latest and assumed that this is the state blocks execute on. Avalanche also folds storage slot S and S with bit 248 flipped into one entry (finding F-040), and has the thinnest mined evidence of the 21 networks. Task 1: read the SAE code and the RPC backend at that commit. What state do eth_call, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getBalance and debug_traceCall run against for latest, safe, finalized, pending and a block number: the last executed block, the last accepted block before execution, or the last settled state? Can latest name a block whose state does not exist yet, and what does the node answer then? Task 2: which checks does a transaction pass at acceptance (nonce, balance for the worst-case fee, gas limit, access list) and which run only at execution? List every way a transaction of an accepted block can end differently from what the builder assumed: skipped, failed before its first frame, run with a different base fee or gas price, run after a transaction that the builder did not expect before it, or run under a different timestamp, block number, PREVRANDAO or blob base fee than the header implies. For each, say whether the PoolManager can be left with an unlock half applied, with transient storage from an earlier transaction (the executor must clear it per transaction; check the exact call), or with a native transfer made and the rest of the transaction dropped. Check what BLOCKHASH, NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, BASEFEE, GASPRICE, COINBASE, SELFBALANCE and GAS return during delayed execution. The PoolManager reads SELFBALANCE and GAS (src/types/Currency.sol:48, :73, :92; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134); hooks read the others. Task 3: can an ordinary account use the gap between acceptance and execution against another user: a transaction that is accepted, then executes after the state it was priced against has changed, a withdrawal whose receipt a wallet or bridge reads before execution has happened, or a receipt or log served for a block whose execution later differs? Read how receipts and logs are served for accepted blocks that are not executed yet. Task 4: mined evidence. Replay the newest 20,000 PoolManager transactions on Avalanche (0x06380c0e0912312b5150364b9dc4542ba0dbbc85 is the address used in earlier cycles; confirm it by code) with the cycle 23 scripts, including blocks produced since the SAE activation, and compare the committed state after each block with the replay (cycle 23 committed.py). Add the failed and log-free transactions with the cycle 24 scripts (research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-failed-tx-replay.work). Give the activation block or time of SAE on mainnet from a primary source and the split of replayed transactions before and after it. Task 5: is Firewood the C-Chain database at this release, and does its key encoding add any rule below the bit 248 transform (lead L-1072)? Rerun the cycle 24 transient and persistent fold probe (research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-storage-key-mapping.work) on Avalanche at latest, safe and finalized and compare the three answers.
